claims.claim: Customer concentration is a current execution and collection risk: at June 30, 2026 two customers were 27% and 23% of accounts receivable; two customers were 25% and 17% of Q2 revenue.

The company states software renewal/expansion, drug-discovery collaboration success, AI/ML use, and operating-result volatility remain principal risks; these constrain any inference that Bunsen adoption alone proves durable economics.

causalEdges.mechanism: a small number of customers represent material shares of quarterly revenue and receivables
renewal, expansion and measurable customer value must persist before adoption becomes durable recurring economics

risks: Material customer concentration can amplify timing, renewal and collection volatility.
AI/ML product adoption does not by itself establish scientific superiority, renewal durability or economic value capture.
unknowns: Current evidence does not quantify Bunsen-specific renewal, expansion, productivity uplift or customer-level economics.

gatingStatus.note: Source-addressed risk support only; Alpha retains numeric underwriting authority.

recommendedNextStateOwner.action: Incorporate source-addressed concentration and execution risks into Alpha risk evidence without treating Beta as a numeric score.
